# Pixel Dojo clarifies Sensei’s standing budgets, larger approvals and retake decisions


By OpenTools Team


The October 31 documentation update distinguishes jobs within a set budget from larger approvals, and remakes from flagged takes.


##


A budget is not another click


The[Sensei FAQ](https://pixeldojo.ai/sensei) says small jobs run within a set budget, while larger ones wait for Approve. That qualifies its broader no‑spending‑without‑asking language: prior budget authorization is different from a fresh click for every small job. Users can stop the run; the page does not define the numerical small‑job threshold.


##


Recovery still involves choices


Pixel Dojo says images and videos use[normal generation credits plus a small Sensei thinking fee](https://pixeldojo.ai/sensei) . It does not give a fixed price for every recovery attempt.


The[October 31 changelog](https://pixeldojo.ai/changelog) clarifies that a take missing the brief is remade or flagged for the user to decide. The[product page](https://pixeldojo.ai/sensei) repeats that choice; it does not establish free, unlimited retakes or remove the user’s judgment.


Archival photograph of director Richard Farmer on location for Under God in Los Angeles; not Pixel Dojo staff or a Sensei result.
